cfc577ee24cf.en: Here are two loops that add up n numbers. <bookmark mark='a'/> The first walks an array in order. <bookmark mark='b'/> The second follows a linked list whose nodes are scattered through memory. <bookmark mark='c'/> Both do n additions, both are linear time, and they compute the same sum. Every analysis in Parts 16 to 23 would call them equal. <bookmark mark='d'/> The machine does not. The array streams through the caches a line at a time, with the prefetcher running ahead, while each list node is a separate trip to memory that cannot start until the previous one has returned.
cfc577ee24cf.zh: 这里有两个把 n 个数加起来的循环。<bookmark mark='a'/>第一个按顺序遍历一个数组。<bookmark mark='b'/>第二个沿着一个链表走，链表的节点散落在内存各处。<bookmark mark='c'/>两者都做 n 次加法，都是线性时间，算出的和也一样。第16到第23部分的每一种分析都会说它们相等。<bookmark mark='d'/>机器却不这么认为。数组一行一行地流过缓存，预取器跑在前面；而链表的每个节点都是一次单独的内存访问，要等上一次返回之后才能开始。

86f390aeb096.en: Here they are, timed on the machine that made this video. <bookmark mark='a'/> With a thousand elements everything fits in the first-level cache, and the list is already five times slower. <bookmark mark='b'/> At sixty-five thousand it is twenty-two times slower. <bookmark mark='c'/> At sixteen million the array costs a nanosecond and a half per element and the list two hundred: a hundred and forty times apart, with the same big-O. <bookmark mark='d'/> Big-O hides the constant factor, and on real hardware the constant is mostly the memory hierarchy of Part 9. This part is about the tools that real code is built from, and about engineering them for the machine.
86f390aeb096.zh: 这是在制作这段视频的机器上的计时。<bookmark mark='a'/>一千个元素时，一切都装得进一级缓存，链表已经慢了五倍。<bookmark mark='b'/>六万五千个时，慢了二十二倍。<bookmark mark='c'/>一千六百万个时，数组每个元素一纳秒半，链表两百纳秒：相差一百四十倍，而大 O 相同。<bookmark mark='d'/>大 O 隐藏了常数因子，而在真实硬件上，这个常数主要就是第9部分的存储层次。这一部分讲的是真实代码赖以构建的工具，以及如何为机器而对它们做工程优化。

655c444ccaed.en: Part 24 of Computer Science, Built: Algorithms in Practice. <bookmark mark='a'/> In this part: the everyday data structures of real code, prefix sums, Fenwick and segment trees, range minimum and lowest common ancestors; the linear-time patterns, two pointers, monotonic stacks and binary search on the answer; word-level tricks and the Four Russians; meet in the middle and square roots; then algorithm engineering, measured on this machine: memory layouts, vector instructions, hash tables and sorting; how to benchmark honestly; and the Job, engineered, for the ledger's tenth row.
655c444ccaed.zh: 计算机科学，从零搭建，第24部分：实践中的算法。<bookmark mark='a'/>这一部分包括：真实代码中的日常数据结构，前缀和、Fenwick 树与线段树、区间最小值与最近公共祖先；线性时间的套路，双指针、单调栈与二分答案；字级技巧与四个俄罗斯人算法；折半搜索与平方根分块；然后是在这台机器上测量的算法工程：内存布局、向量指令、哈希表与排序；如何诚实地做基准测试；以及经过工程优化的 Job，填上账本的第十行。

bf68bc34b8ec.en: The simplest precomputation in the business. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here are sixteen numbers, and we will be asked, over and over, for the sum of some stretch of them. <bookmark mark='b'/> Walk the array once and write down the running totals: S of i is the sum of everything before position i. <bookmark mark='c'/> Now any range sum is one subtraction. Positions three to ten: the total up to eleven, minus the total up to three, forty-four minus eight, thirty-six. <bookmark mark='d'/> Linear work once, then constant work per question. Nearly every index in this part makes some version of that trade.
bf68bc34b8ec.zh: 这一行里最简单的预计算。<bookmark mark='a'/>这里有十六个数，我们会被反复问到其中某一段的和。<bookmark mark='b'/>把数组走一遍，记下累计和：S i 是位置 i 之前所有元素的和。<bookmark mark='c'/>现在任何一段的和都只是一次减法。位置三到十：到十一为止的总和，减去到三为止的总和，四十四减八，三十六。<bookmark mark='d'/>一次线性的工作，然后每个问题常数时间。这一部分里几乎每一种索引都在做某种形式的这种交换。

a534404f553e.en: Run the idea backwards and it handles updates. <bookmark mark='a'/> Suppose we must add three to positions two to nine, two to positions five to twelve, and one to positions zero to four. Doing it directly touches every position in every range. <bookmark mark='b'/> Instead keep a difference array: for each update, add the amount where its range starts and subtract it just after the range ends. Two cells per update, however long the range. <bookmark mark='c'/> One prefix sum at the end rebuilds the array: the running total switches each update on at its start and off after its end. <bookmark mark='d'/> In two dimensions the same trick costs four corners per rectangle.
a534404f553e.zh: 把这个想法倒过来用，它就能处理更新。<bookmark mark='a'/>假设要给位置二到九加三，给位置五到十二加二，给位置零到四加一。直接做，就要碰到每个区间里的每个位置。<bookmark mark='b'/>改用差分数组：对每次更新，在区间开始处加上这个量，在区间结束之后紧接着减去它。每次更新两个单元，无论区间多长。<bookmark mark='c'/>最后做一次前缀和就重建出数组：累计和在每次更新的起点把它打开，在终点之后把它关上。<bookmark mark='d'/>在二维中，同样的技巧每个矩形只需四个角。

2293bb78c7a6.en: Prefix sums work in two dimensions. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is a small image. <bookmark mark='b'/> Its integral image stores, at each position, the sum of every pixel above and to the left. One pass builds it. <bookmark mark='c'/> Then the sum over any rectangle is four lookups: the corner below and to the right, minus the two strips we do not want, plus the corner we subtracted twice. <bookmark mark='d'/> Paul Viola and Michael Jones built real-time face detection on this in 2001: thousands of rectangle features per window, each in constant time, as the AI series showed. Frank Crow had used the same tables in 1984 to blur textures in computer graphics.
2293bb78c7a6.zh: 前缀和在二维中同样适用。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是一幅小图像。<bookmark mark='b'/>它的积分图在每个位置存储其左上方所有像素之和，扫一遍就能建好。<bookmark mark='c'/>于是任何矩形内的和都是四次查表：右下角的值，减去不需要的两条，再加回被减了两次的那个角。<bookmark mark='d'/>Paul Viola 和 Michael Jones 在2001年用它做出了实时人脸检测：每个窗口几千个矩形特征，每个都是常数时间，正如 AI 系列所展示的。Frank Crow 早在1984年就在计算机图形学中用同样的表来模糊纹理。

f1b3ecb6d864.en: One more property makes prefix sums a workhorse: they parallelize, although each total seems to depend on the one before. <bookmark mark='a'/> In the first round, every element adds its left neighbour. <bookmark mark='b'/> In the second, every element adds the value two places to its left; in the third, four places. <bookmark mark='c'/> After log n rounds every position holds its prefix sum, and each round is done by all elements at once. Daniel Hillis and Guy Steele ran this on the Connection Machine, and Guy Blelloch made it work-efficient. <bookmark mark='d'/> Graphics cards use scans to compact streams, to sort, and to handle sparse matrices.
f1b3ecb6d864.zh: 还有一个性质让前缀和成为主力：它能并行，尽管每个累计和看起来都依赖前一个。<bookmark mark='a'/>第一轮，每个元素加上它左边的邻居。<bookmark mark='b'/>第二轮，每个元素加上左边隔两个位置的值；第三轮，隔四个位置。<bookmark mark='c'/>经过 log n 轮，每个位置都持有它的前缀和，而每一轮都由所有元素同时完成。Daniel Hillis 和 Guy Steele 在连接机上这样运行它，Guy Blelloch 让它做到了工作量最优。<bookmark mark='d'/>显卡用扫描来压缩数据流、排序和处理稀疏矩阵。

b858303be8d8.en: Prefix sums answer in constant time, but one update can force n of them to change. Peter Fenwick's tree of 1994 balances the two, with one array and two loops. <bookmark mark='a'/> Cell i stores the sum of a range ending at i whose length is the lowest set bit of i. Odd cells hold one element; cells that are multiples of two but not four hold two; multiples of four, four; and so on. <bookmark mark='b'/> The lowest set bit is i and minus i, in two's complement, the trick from Part 4. <bookmark mark='c'/> To sum the first thirteen elements, take cell thirteen, then strip its lowest bit to get twelve, then eight, and stop at zero. Three cells cover one to thirteen exactly. <bookmark mark='d'/> To add to element five, update every cell whose range contains five: add the lowest bit instead. Five, six, eight, sixteen.
b858303be8d8.zh: 前缀和能常数时间回答，但一次更新可能迫使 n 个前缀和改变。Peter Fenwick 1994年的树在两者之间取得平衡，只用一个数组和两个循环。<bookmark mark='a'/>单元 i 存储一个以 i 结尾的区间之和，区间长度是 i 的最低置位比特。奇数单元存一个元素；是二的倍数但不是四的倍数的单元存两个；四的倍数存四个；依此类推。<bookmark mark='b'/>最低置位比特就是 i 与负 i 按位与，在补码中成立，这是第4部分的技巧。<bookmark mark='c'/>要求前十三个元素的和，取单元十三，再去掉它的最低比特得到十二，然后是八，到零为止。三个单元恰好覆盖一到十三。<bookmark mark='d'/>要给第五个元素加上一个值，就更新每个区间包含五的单元：改为加上最低比特。五、六、八、十六。

1778c8f17201.en: Why is it right, and why fast? <bookmark mark='a'/> A query clears one set bit of i each step, so it takes at most log n steps, and the ranges it visits sit end to end, covering one to i exactly once. <bookmark mark='b'/> An update adds the lowest set bit, which pushes that bit at least one place to the left, so it too takes at most log n steps, and it visits exactly the cells whose ranges contain i. <bookmark mark='c'/> The two loops read the same binary representation in opposite directions. <bookmark mark='d'/> Measured on random operations, the cells touched grow by one each time n is multiplied by four: about half of log n on average, because a random number has half its bits set.
1778c8f17201.zh: 它为什么正确，又为什么快？<bookmark mark='a'/>查询每一步清除 i 的一个置位比特，所以至多 log n 步，而它访问的区间首尾相接，恰好覆盖一到 i 各一次。<bookmark mark='b'/>更新加上最低置位比特，把这一位至少向左推一位，所以也至多 log n 步，而它访问的恰好是区间包含 i 的那些单元。<bookmark mark='c'/>两个循环是在相反方向上读同一个二进制表示。<bookmark mark='d'/>在随机操作上测量，n 每乘以四，访问的单元数就多一个：平均约为 log n 的一半，因为一个随机数有一半的比特是一。

d9bf4d30bfcb.en: How do they compare on a real machine? <bookmark mark='a'/> A million numbers, a million random operations, half updates and half prefix queries, in C. <bookmark mark='b'/> The Fenwick tree takes about fifty nanoseconds an operation, nearly three times faster than a segment tree, because it is one array of n cells with no recursion and no wasted nodes. <bookmark mark='c'/> The naive structures, constant time on one operation and linear on the other, take well over a hundred thousand. Here the asymptotics really do decide. <bookmark mark='d'/> Fenwick designed his tree for the frequency tables of arithmetic coding; order books and game leaderboards use it today.
d9bf4d30bfcb.zh: 它们在真实机器上比较起来如何？<bookmark mark='a'/>一百万个数，一百万次随机操作，一半更新一半前缀查询，用 C 语言。<bookmark mark='b'/>Fenwick 树每次操作大约五十纳秒，比线段树快将近三倍，因为它是一个 n 个单元的数组，没有递归，也没有浪费的节点。<bookmark mark='c'/>两种朴素结构，一种操作常数时间、另一种线性时间，要远远超过十万纳秒。在这里，渐近复杂度确实起了决定作用。<bookmark mark='d'/>Fenwick 设计这棵树是为了算术编码的频率表；如今订单簿和游戏排行榜都在用它。

a45c8d01e492.en: Fenwick trees need an operation you can undo, like subtraction. For the minimum of a range you cannot subtract, and you need a segment tree. <bookmark mark='a'/> Build a balanced tree over the array. Each node holds the minimum of the stretch below it: the leaves are the elements, the root the whole array. Any associative operation works the same way. <bookmark mark='b'/> To answer positions three to twelve, descend from the root and stop at every node whose range lies entirely inside the query. Four nodes cover this range. At most two per level ever do, so a query costs logarithmic time. <bookmark mark='c'/> Changing one element changes only the nodes above it, one per level. <bookmark mark='d'/> Minimum, maximum, greatest common divisor, matrix products: anything associative. Even the maximum subarray sum, if each node keeps four numbers instead of one.
a45c8d01e492.zh: Fenwick 树需要一个可以撤销的运算，比如减法。区间最小值无法相减，这时就需要线段树。<bookmark mark='a'/>在数组之上建一棵平衡树。每个节点保存它下面那一段的最小值：叶子是各个元素，根是整个数组。任何满足结合律的运算都一样。<bookmark mark='b'/>要回答位置三到十二，从根往下走，在每个区间完全落在查询之内的节点处停下。四个节点覆盖了这个区间。每层至多两个，所以一次查询是对数时间。<bookmark mark='c'/>改变一个元素，只会改变它上方的节点，每层一个。<bookmark mark='d'/>最小值、最大值、最大公约数、矩阵乘积：任何满足结合律的东西都行。甚至最大子段和，只要每个节点存四个数而不是一个。

8117eb47f541.en: The trick that makes segment trees so flexible is that a node can carry a small record instead of one number. <bookmark mark='a'/> Take the maximum-sum stretch of consecutive elements, the problem Bentley made famous. For each half, keep four numbers: its total, its best prefix, its best suffix, and its best stretch anywhere. <bookmark mark='b'/> Two halves combine in constant time. The total adds. The best prefix is either the left's, or the whole left plus the right's best prefix, and the suffix is the mirror image. <bookmark mark='c'/> And the best stretch lies in the left half, in the right half, or across the middle, where it is the left's best suffix joined to the right's best prefix. Here the winner is the one that crosses: six, which brute force confirms. <bookmark mark='d'/> Because this combination is associative, the segment tree can answer the maximum subarray of any range, while elements change underneath it.
8117eb47f541.zh: 让线段树如此灵活的诀窍在于，一个节点可以存一个小记录，而不是一个数。<bookmark mark='a'/>以 Bentley 使之出名的最大连续子段和为例。对每一半保存四个数：总和、最好的前缀、最好的后缀，以及任意位置最好的一段。<bookmark mark='b'/>两半在常数时间内合并。总和相加。最好的前缀要么是左半的，要么是整个左半加上右半最好的前缀；后缀与之对称。<bookmark mark='c'/>而最好的一段要么在左半，要么在右半，要么跨过中点，此时它是左半最好的后缀接上右半最好的前缀。这里胜出的是跨过中点的那一段：六，暴力搜索也确认了。<bookmark mark='d'/>因为这种合并满足结合律，线段树就能回答任意区间的最大子段和，同时元素还在下面不断变化。

f9fa64dcd051.en: What if the updates are ranges too? <bookmark mark='a'/> To add a value to every element from l to r, descend as a query does, and at each covering node, update its summary and leave a tag saying: everything below me owes this amount. <bookmark mark='b'/> The tag is pushed to the children only when a later query or update has to go beneath it. That laziness is the whole trick. <bookmark mark='c'/> On random ranges, touching every element costs about a quarter of n per update; the lazy tree visits a few dozen nodes, growing with the logarithm. <bookmark mark='d'/> And because an update changes only one path of nodes, you can copy that path instead of overwriting it, and keep every past version of the array, queryable, for the price of a logarithm per update. That is a persistent segment tree.
f9fa64dcd051.zh: 如果更新也是区间呢？<bookmark mark='a'/>要给从 l 到 r 的每个元素加上一个值，像查询一样往下走，在每个覆盖节点处更新它的汇总，并留下一个标记：我下面的每个元素都欠这么多。<bookmark mark='b'/>只有当后来的查询或更新需要走到它下面时，才把标记下推给孩子。这种懒惰就是全部的诀窍。<bookmark mark='c'/>在随机区间上，逐个修改元素每次更新大约要 n 的四分之一；懒惰的树只访问几十个节点，随对数增长。<bookmark mark='d'/>而且因为一次更新只改变一条路径上的节点，你可以复制这条路径而不是覆盖它，从而以每次更新一个对数的代价，保留数组的每一个历史版本，随时可查。这就是可持久化线段树。

7e78ba4157f0.en: Chapter four. Range minimum, and lowest common ancestors.
7e78ba4157f0.zh: 第4章。区间最小值，与最近公共祖先。

4e792c6226c3.en: If the array never changes, a range minimum can be a single lookup. <bookmark mark='a'/> Precompute the minimum of every window whose length is a power of two. Row zero is the array itself; each row is built from the one above, the smaller of two neighbouring windows. That is n log n numbers. <bookmark mark='b'/> To answer positions two to twelve, a range of eleven, take the largest power of two that fits, eight, and look up two windows of length eight: one starting at the left end, one ending at the right end. <bookmark mark='c'/> They overlap, and for the minimum that does not matter, because the minimum of a number with itself is that number. <bookmark mark='d'/> For a sum the overlap would be counted twice, which is why sums use the trees of the last two chapters.
4e792c6226c3.zh: 如果数组从不改变，区间最小值可以只是一次查表。<bookmark mark='a'/>预先算出每个长度为二的幂的窗口的最小值。第零行就是数组本身；每一行都由上一行算出，取两个相邻窗口中较小的那个。总共 n log n 个数。<bookmark mark='b'/>要回答位置二到十二，一段长为十一的区间，取能放得下的最大的二的幂，八，查两个长度为八的窗口：一个从左端开始，一个在右端结束。<bookmark mark='c'/>它们重叠了，而对最小值来说这无关紧要，因为一个数与它自己的最小值就是它本身。<bookmark mark='d'/>对于求和，重叠部分会被算两次，这就是为什么求和要用前两章的树。

07f052c8b73f.en: In a rooted tree, the lowest common ancestor of two nodes is the deepest node above both. <bookmark mark='a'/> Walk around the tree, writing down each node every time you pass it, with its depth. <bookmark mark='b'/> Between the first visits of nodes seven and four, the tour must climb to their common ancestor and no higher, so the shallowest node in that stretch is the answer: node one. <bookmark mark='c'/> Lowest common ancestor is range minimum on the depths, and the sparse table answers it in constant time. <bookmark mark='d'/> The other classic is binary lifting: store each node's ancestor two to the j levels up. Lift the deeper node to the same depth, then lift both by decreasing powers of two while they differ. Version control finds the merge base of two branches this way, as Part 41 will show.
07f052c8b73f.zh: 在一棵有根树中，两个节点的最近公共祖先是同时位于两者之上的最深的节点。<bookmark mark='a'/>绕着树走一圈，每经过一个节点就把它和它的深度记下来。<bookmark mark='b'/>在节点七和节点四第一次被访问之间，这次巡游必须爬到它们的公共祖先，而不会更高，所以这一段中最浅的节点就是答案：节点一。<bookmark mark='c'/>最近公共祖先就是深度上的区间最小值，稀疏表能常数时间回答它。<bookmark mark='d'/>另一种经典做法是倍增：存下每个节点向上二的 j 次方层的祖先。先把较深的节点提到同一深度，再在两者不同时按递减的二的幂把两者一起往上提。版本控制就是这样找出两个分支的合并基点的，第41部分会讲到。

30044482ec6f.en: The reduction runs the other way as well. <bookmark mark='a'/> The Cartesian tree of an array puts the minimum at the root, builds the left part's tree to its left and the right part's to its right, and so on down. <bookmark mark='b'/> One left-to-right pass with a stack builds it, the monotonic stack of the next chapter. <bookmark mark='c'/> The minimum of any range of the array is the lowest common ancestor of its two ends in this tree. So range minimum and lowest common ancestor are the same problem. <bookmark mark='d'/> Michael Bender and Martín Farach-Colton used the two reductions together to reach linear preprocessing and constant queries, and Johannes Fischer and Volker Heun squeezed the structure into two bits per element.
30044482ec6f.zh: 这种归约反过来也成立。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个数组的 Cartesian 树把最小值放在根上，把左边部分的树建在它左边、右边部分的树建在它右边，如此递归下去。<bookmark mark='b'/>从左到右用一个栈扫一遍就能建好，用的正是下一章的单调栈。<bookmark mark='c'/>数组任意区间的最小值，就是这棵树中区间两端的最近公共祖先。所以区间最小值和最近公共祖先是同一个问题。<bookmark mark='d'/>Michael Bender 和 Martín Farach-Colton 把两种归约结合起来，做到了线性预处理、常数查询；Johannes Fischer 和 Volker Heun 则把这个结构压缩到每个元素两比特。

05c79222c23c.en: Chapter five. Two pointers, and monotonic stacks.

157b9d31d80c.en: Slide a window of four along an array and report the largest value in each position of the window. Checking all four each time costs n times k. <bookmark mark='a'/> Keep instead a double-ended queue of positions whose values decrease from front to back. When a new value arrives, every smaller value at the back can never be a window's maximum again, because the newcomer is larger and will stay longer; pop them. <bookmark mark='b'/> When the front falls out of the window, drop it. The front is always the current maximum. <bookmark mark='c'/> Each position enters the queue once and leaves at most once, so the whole pass is linear, however wide the window. <bookmark mark='d'/> This is the two-pointer pattern: both ends of the window only move forward. The inner loop looks quadratic, and the amortized count proves it linear.
157b9d31d80c.zh: 让一个宽为四的窗口沿数组滑动，在窗口的每个位置报告其中最大的值。每次都检查四个，代价是 n 乘以 k。<bookmark mark='a'/>改为维护一个双端队列，存放从前到后值递减的位置。新值到来时，队尾每个更小的值都再也不可能成为某个窗口的最大值，因为新来的更大，而且会待得更久；把它们弹出。<bookmark mark='b'/>当队首滑出窗口时，丢掉它。队首永远是当前的最大值。<bookmark mark='c'/>每个位置进队一次、至多出队一次，所以整个扫描是线性的，与窗口多宽无关。<bookmark mark='d'/>这就是双指针模式：窗口的两端都只向前移动。内层循环看起来是平方的，均摊计数证明它是线性的。

a1de196840a0.en: The window need not have a fixed width. <bookmark mark='a'/> Find the longest stretch of this string with no repeated letter. Move the right end one letter at a time. When the new letter already occurs inside the window, jump the left end to just past that earlier occurrence. <bookmark mark='b'/> A table of each letter's last position makes every move constant time, and the left end never moves backwards. <bookmark mark='c'/> So the whole scan is at most two n pointer moves, where checking every window would be quadratic. <bookmark mark='d'/> The same two-pointer skeleton finds the smallest window containing a set of words, or the longest subarray whose sum stays under a budget.
a1de196840a0.zh: 窗口的宽度不必固定。<bookmark mark='a'/>找出这个字符串中没有重复字母的最长一段。右端每次前进一个字母。当新字母已经出现在窗口内时，把左端跳到那次出现的紧后面。<bookmark mark='b'/>用一张记录每个字母上次位置的表，每次移动都是常数时间，而左端从不后退。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以整个扫描至多 2n 次指针移动，而检查每个窗口则是平方的。<bookmark mark='d'/>同样的双指针骨架还能找出包含一组单词的最小窗口，或者和不超过预算的最长子数组。

419cca518a37.en: A stack can be monotone too. <bookmark mark='a'/> For each element, find the next element to its right that is larger. Keep a stack of positions still waiting for an answer. Each new value answers every smaller value on top of the stack, pops them, and waits itself. <bookmark mark='b'/> The waiting values are always in decreasing order, and each position is pushed and popped once: linear time again. <bookmark mark='c'/> The famous application is the largest rectangle under a histogram. When a bar is popped, the bar that popped it is the first lower bar to its right, and the bar beneath it on the stack is the first lower bar to its left. Between them lies the widest rectangle of that bar's height. <bookmark mark='d'/> Here the best has height four across four bars, area sixteen, and brute force agrees. <bookmark mark='e'/> Stock spans, trapped rain water and the skyline problem are the same stack in different clothes.
419cca518a37.zh: 栈也可以是单调的。<bookmark mark='a'/>对每个元素，找出它右边第一个更大的元素。维护一个仍在等待答案的位置栈。每个新值回答栈顶所有比它小的值，把它们弹出，然后自己入栈等待。<bookmark mark='b'/>等待中的值总是递减的，每个位置压入、弹出各一次：又是线性时间。<bookmark mark='c'/>著名的应用是直方图中的最大矩形。当一根柱子被弹出时，弹出它的那根是它右边第一根更矮的柱子，栈中它下面那根是它左边第一根更矮的柱子。两者之间就是这根柱子高度下最宽的矩形。<bookmark mark='d'/>这里最好的高为四、横跨四根柱子，面积十六，暴力搜索也一致。<bookmark mark='e'/>股票跨度、接雨水和天际线问题，都是换了衣服的同一个栈。

9ea6ee7a803c.en: Chapter six. Searching for the answer.

7eb9eeaff887.en: Binary search works on anything monotone, not just arrays. <bookmark mark='a'/> Ten packages must be shipped in order, within four days. What is the smallest daily capacity that does it? <bookmark mark='b'/> For a given capacity the answer is easy to check: load each day greedily until the next package would not fit. And the answer is monotone: if a capacity works, every larger one works too. <bookmark mark='c'/> So binary-search the boundary between the capacities that fail and the ones that work. Five checks find it: eighteen. <bookmark mark='d'/> This is one of the most useful patterns in practice: minimize the largest load, maximize the smallest gap, find the earliest day something becomes true. <bookmark mark='e'/> And a warning from Knuth: binary search was first published in 1946, and the first version that was correct for every length appeared fourteen years later.
7eb9eeaff887.zh: 二分查找适用于任何单调的东西，而不只是数组。<bookmark mark='a'/>十个包裹必须按顺序在四天内运完。最小的每日运力是多少？<bookmark mark='b'/>对给定的运力，答案很容易检查：每天贪心地装货，直到下一个包裹放不下为止。而且答案是单调的：如果某个运力可行，更大的也都可行。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以在不可行与可行的运力之间二分查找分界线。五次检查就找到了：十八。<bookmark mark='d'/>这是实践中最有用的模式之一：最小化最大负载，最大化最小间隔，找出某件事变为真的最早一天。<bookmark mark='e'/>Knuth 还给出了一个警告：二分查找在1946年首次发表，而第一个对所有长度都正确的版本，十四年后才出现。

4b0fc9d88699.en: Binary search is famous for being easy to get wrong, so here is a version to trust. <bookmark mark='a'/> Keep an invariant: everything to the left of lo is smaller than x, and everything from hi onwards is at least x. Each step shrinks the gap between them, and when it closes, lo is the answer. <bookmark mark='b'/> Use half-open ranges, from lo up to but not including hi, and the plus-or-minus-one guesswork disappears: the empty range is simply lo equal to hi. <bookmark mark='c'/> Compute the middle as lo plus half the difference. Adding lo and hi first overflows a 32-bit integer once an array has a billion elements, a bug Joshua Bloch found in 2006 in Java's own library, where it had sat for nine years. <bookmark mark='d'/> And return the boundary, the first position not less than x, rather than just found or not found. Lower and upper bounds answer counting and range questions too.
4b0fc9d88699.zh: 二分查找以容易写错而闻名，所以这里给出一个值得信赖的版本。<bookmark mark='a'/>保持一个不变式：lo 左边的一切都小于 x，从 hi 起的一切都至少为 x。每一步都缩小两者之间的空隙，空隙闭合时，lo 就是答案。<bookmark mark='b'/>使用半开区间，从 lo 到 hi 但不含 hi，加一减一的猜测就消失了：空区间就是 lo 等于 hi。<bookmark mark='c'/>把中点算成 lo 加上差的一半。先把 lo 和 hi 相加，一旦数组有十亿个元素就会让32位整数溢出；Joshua Bloch 在2006年在 Java 自己的库中发现了这个错误，它已经在那里待了九年。<bookmark mark='d'/>并且返回分界点，即第一个不小于 x 的位置，而不只是找到或没找到。下界和上界还能回答计数和区间问题。

f2a88e3255fd.en: Sometimes you know roughly where the answer is. <bookmark mark='a'/> Galloping, or exponential search, probes one place ahead, then two, four, eight, until it passes the target, and then binary-searches the last gap. <bookmark mark='b'/> If the answer is d places away, that costs about two log d probes, whatever the length of the array. Jon Bentley and Andrew Yao analysed it in 1976. <bookmark mark='c'/> On a million keys it beats plain binary search until the answer is about a thousand places away. <bookmark mark='d'/> That is exactly the situation when merging two sorted runs, which is why Timsort gallops, and when intersecting the posting lists of a search engine. <bookmark mark='e'/> And for the peak of a function that rises and then falls, ternary search throws away a third of the interval at each step.
f2a88e3255fd.zh: 有时你大致知道答案在哪里。<bookmark mark='a'/>倍增查找，也叫指数查找，先向前探一格，再两格、四格、八格，直到越过目标，然后在最后一段中二分查找。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果答案在 d 格之外，代价约为两倍 log d 次探查，与数组的长度无关。Jon Bentley 和姚期智在1976年分析了它。<bookmark mark='c'/>在一百万个键上，只要答案在大约一千格以内，它就胜过普通的二分查找。<bookmark mark='d'/>这正是归并两个有序段时的情形，所以 Timsort 会倍增查找；搜索引擎求倒排表的交集时也是如此。<bookmark mark='e'/>而对于先升后降的函数的峰值，三分查找每一步丢掉区间的三分之一。

bccf23a8cf9b.en: Chapter seven. Bits, and the Four Russians.
bccf23a8cf9b.zh: 第7章。比特，与四个俄罗斯人算法。

9882458425cc.en: A machine word is sixty-four bits, and it is often best read as a set of sixty-four small things. <bookmark mark='a'/> Counting the members is one instruction, popcount; and x and x minus one clears the lowest member, so a loop of that visits each member once. <bookmark mark='b'/> x and minus x isolates the lowest member, the trick behind Fenwick's tree. <bookmark mark='c'/> i exclusive-or i shifted right once is the Gray code, where neighbours differ in a single bit, which is why rotary encoders use it. <bookmark mark='d'/> Union, intersection and membership of small sets become single instructions. <bookmark mark='e'/> Henry Warren's book collects hundreds of these.
9882458425cc.zh: 一个机器字是六十四个比特，通常最好把它看作六十四个小东西的集合。<bookmark mark='a'/>数一数成员只要一条指令，popcount；而 x 与 x 减一按位与会清除最低的成员，所以这样循环就能逐个访问每个成员。<bookmark mark='b'/>x 与负 x 按位与分离出最低的成员，这正是 Fenwick 树背后的技巧。<bookmark mark='c'/>i 与 i 右移一位做异或，就是 Gray 码，相邻两个数只差一个比特，所以旋转编码器使用它。<bookmark mark='d'/>小集合的并、交和成员判断都变成了单条指令。<bookmark mark='e'/>Henry Warren 的书收录了数百个这样的技巧。

117948f948a5.en: Some dynamic programs run over every subset of a set, and need every subset of each subset. <bookmark mark='a'/> These three lines visit every submask of m, from m itself down to zero: subtract one, which borrows through the lowest member, and mask, which throws away what is not in m. <bookmark mark='b'/> Over all masks of n elements the loop body runs three to the n times, not four to the n, because each element is either outside the mask, in the mask but not the submask, or in both. We counted: exactly three to the n, every time. <bookmark mark='c'/> That is the inner loop of dynamic programming over subsets, for partitions, schedules and Steiner trees.
117948f948a5.zh: 有些动态规划要遍历一个集合的每个子集，而且需要每个子集的每个子集。<bookmark mark='a'/>这三行代码访问 m 的每个子掩码，从 m 本身直到零：减一，借位穿过最低的成员；再按位与，丢掉不在 m 中的部分。<bookmark mark='b'/>对 n 个元素的所有掩码，循环体恰好运行三的 n 次方次，而不是四的 n 次方次，因为每个元素要么在掩码之外，要么在掩码中但不在子掩码中，要么两者都在。我们数过：每次都恰好是三的 n 次方。<bookmark mark='c'/>这就是子集动态规划的内层循环，用于集合划分、调度和 Steiner 树。

9b0c925f5247.en: In 1970 four Soviet mathematicians, Arlazarov, Dinic, Kronrod and Faradzev, noticed that a computer can process a whole word of bits in one step, and shaved a logarithm off boolean matrix problems. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is their idea at work on this machine. <bookmark mark='b'/> Warshall's transitive closure, with each row of the reachability matrix packed into words, ORs sixty-four columns at once; the compiler already vectorized the byte version, and the bitset version is still about ten times faster. <bookmark mark='c'/> The longest common subsequence of two strings is a quadratic dynamic program, but one row of it can be computed with a few word operations: an addition propagates the carries along the row. On two strings of twenty thousand letters, that is over a hundred times faster, with the same answer. <bookmark mark='d'/> The same trick runs inside diff, DNA aligners and the approximate matcher agrep.
9b0c925f5247.zh: 1970年，四位苏联数学家，Arlazarov、Dinic、Kronrod 和 Faradzev，注意到计算机一步就能处理一整个字的比特，从而让布尔矩阵问题省掉了一个对数因子。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是他们的想法在这台机器上的效果。<bookmark mark='b'/>Warshall 的传递闭包，把可达矩阵的每一行打包成字，一次对六十四列做或运算；编译器已经把按字节的版本向量化了，而按比特集的版本仍然快了大约十倍。<bookmark mark='c'/>两个字符串的最长公共子序列是一个平方的动态规划，但它的一行可以用几次字运算算出：一次加法让进位沿着这一行传播。在两个两万个字母的字符串上，快了一百多倍，答案相同。<bookmark mark='d'/>同样的技巧运行在 diff、DNA 比对工具和近似匹配工具 agrep 之中。

284aea72499c.en: Chapter eight. Meet in the middle, and square roots.
284aea72499c.zh: 第8章。折半搜索，与平方根分块。

0a4dfca035c9.en: Some exponential problems can be made exponentially smaller. <bookmark mark='a'/> Subset sum asks whether some of n numbers add up to a target. It is NP-complete, as Part 26 will prove, and trying every subset costs two to the n. <bookmark mark='b'/> Split the numbers into two halves. List every subset sum of the first half, and every subset sum of the second half, sorted. For each sum s on the left, binary-search the right for the target minus s. Ellis Horowitz and Sartaj Sahni did this in 1974: two to the n over two, times n. <bookmark mark='c'/> On twenty numbers, brute force generated a million sums in seventy milliseconds; the middle found the same answer in a fraction of a millisecond. <bookmark mark='d'/> At forty numbers it is a trillion subsets against two million sums. Still exponential, but the square root of it. <bookmark mark='e'/> The same move computes discrete logarithms in Part 30, breaks double encryption in Part 29, and runs a shortest-path search from both ends.
0a4dfca035c9.zh: 有些指数级的问题可以变得指数级地小。<bookmark mark='a'/>子集和问题问：n 个数中是否有一些加起来等于目标值。它是 NP 完全的，第26部分会证明，而尝试每个子集要花二的 n 次方。<bookmark mark='b'/>把这些数分成两半。列出前一半的每个子集和，以及后一半的每个子集和并排好序。对左边的每个和 s，在右边二分查找目标减去 s。Ellis Horowitz 和 Sartaj Sahni 在1974年这样做了：二的 n 除以二次方，再乘以 n。<bookmark mark='c'/>在二十个数上，暴力搜索用七十毫秒生成了一百万个和；折半搜索在不到一毫秒内找到了同样的答案。<bookmark mark='d'/>到四十个数时，就是一万亿个子集对两百万个和。仍然是指数的，但只是它的平方根。<bookmark mark='e'/>同样的一步在第30部分计算离散对数，在第29部分攻破双重加密，还能从两端同时做最短路径搜索。

22956850c11c.en: The square root is the other way to split. <bookmark mark='a'/> Cut the array into about root n blocks of root n elements each, and keep every block's total. <bookmark mark='b'/> A range query adds up the whole blocks in its middle and the single elements at its two ends: about root n steps. A range of eight and a half thousand elements in blocks of a hundred took a hundred and eighty-nine steps. <bookmark mark='c'/> It is cruder than a tree, and more flexible: almost any operation can be kept per block. <bookmark mark='d'/> Mo's algorithm uses the same idea on time. Given all the queries in advance, sort them by the block of their left end, then by their right end, and answer them in that order, moving two pointers and keeping a running answer. <bookmark mark='e'/> For the number of distinct values in twenty thousand ranges, that took two million pointer moves, against eighty-four million elements if each range were scanned on its own.
22956850c11c.zh: 平方根是另一种切分方式。<bookmark mark='a'/>把数组切成大约根号 n 个块，每块根号 n 个元素，并保存每块的总和。<bookmark mark='b'/>一次区间查询把中间的整块加起来，再加上两端的零散元素：大约根号 n 步。一个八千五百个元素的区间，在大小为一百的块中，用了一百八十九步。<bookmark mark='c'/>它比树粗糙，却更灵活：几乎任何运算都可以按块维护。<bookmark mark='d'/>莫队算法把同样的思想用在时间上。事先拿到全部查询，按左端点所在的块排序，再按右端点排序，按这个顺序回答，移动两个指针并维护一个当前答案。<bookmark mark='e'/>对两万个区间中不同值的个数，这用了两百万次指针移动，而如果每个区间单独扫描，要扫八千四百万个元素。

5c560efae3b9.en: Chapter nine. Algorithm engineering, part one: layouts.

e2a67628e685.en: Binary search is optimal in comparisons, and on a large array it is slow, for the reason of the opening chapter. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here are fifteen sorted keys and the probes for one hundred and ten: the middle, then a quarter of the way along, and so on. On a big array every early probe lands on a different cache line, far from the last. <bookmark mark='b'/> The Eytzinger layout, named after a sixteenth-century genealogist who numbered ancestors this way, stores the implicit search tree breadth-first: the root, then its two children, then four grandchildren. Node k's children sit at two k and two k plus one. The top levels are packed together and stay in cache, and the next few levels of any path lie in one predictable region, so the program can prefetch them before it knows which way it will go. <bookmark mark='c'/> Or pack sixteen keys into each sixty-four-byte node, a B-tree in an array, and compare a query against all sixteen with one vector instruction. <bookmark mark='d'/> Paul-Virgile Khuong and Pat Morin measured these layouts in 2017; here they are on this machine.
e2a67628e685.zh: 二分查找在比较次数上是最优的，而在大数组上它很慢，原因就是开头那一章讲的。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是十五个有序的键，以及查找一百一十时的探查：先是中间，然后是四分之一处，依此类推。在大数组上，每一次早期的探查都落在不同的缓存行上，离上一次很远。<bookmark mark='b'/>Eytzinger 布局得名于一位十六世纪的家谱学家，他就是这样给祖先编号的；它按广度优先存储隐式的搜索树：先是根，然后是它的两个孩子，再是四个孙子。节点 k 的孩子位于 2k 和 2k 加一。顶部的几层紧挨在一起，留在缓存中；任何一条路径上接下来几层都位于一个可预测的区域，所以程序可以在知道往哪边走之前就预取它们。<bookmark mark='c'/>或者把十六个键装进每个六十四字节的节点，一棵放在数组里的 B 树，用一条向量指令把查询与全部十六个键比较。<bookmark mark='d'/>Paul-Virgile Khuong 和 Pat Morin 在2017年测量了这些布局；这里是它们在这台机器上的表现。

4304c8ff03ba.en: A million random searches at each size, from a thousand keys to sixty-four million. <bookmark mark='a'/> Plain binary search climbs from seventy nanoseconds to nine hundred as the array outgrows each cache. <bookmark mark='b'/> On this processor the branch-free version is barely faster: the cost is the memory, not mispredicted branches. That differs between machines, which is why you measure. <bookmark mark='c'/> The Eytzinger layout with prefetching is three to four times faster at every size. <bookmark mark='d'/> And the B-tree layout, sixteen keys compared at once, is fastest of all: about five times faster than the textbook at sixty-four million keys. <bookmark mark='e'/> Every one of them makes about log n comparisons. The layout changes nothing in the model of Part 16, and everything on the machine.
4304c8ff03ba.zh: 每种规模一百万次随机查找，从一千个键到六千四百万个。<bookmark mark='a'/>随着数组依次超出每一级缓存，普通的二分查找从七十纳秒攀升到九百纳秒。<bookmark mark='b'/>在这个处理器上，无分支的版本几乎没有更快：代价在于内存，而不是分支预测失败。不同的机器情况不同，这就是为什么要测量。<bookmark mark='c'/>带预取的 Eytzinger 布局在每种规模上都快三到四倍。<bookmark mark='d'/>而 B 树布局，一次比较十六个键，是最快的：在六千四百万个键时，比教科书版本快大约五倍。<bookmark mark='e'/>它们每一个都做大约 log n 次比较。布局在第16部分的模型里什么也没改变，在机器上却改变了一切。

ceda3a74afd0.en: Branch-free search did not help this processor, but that does not mean branches are free. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is a loop that adds up the bytes of an array that are at least a hundred and twenty-eight, with an if. <bookmark mark='b'/> On shuffled data that if is a coin flip. The predictor of Parts 7 and 8 guesses wrong half the time, and every wrong guess throws away the work the pipeline did speculatively. On sorted data the branch goes one way and then the other, and is almost always predicted. The same loop, the same values, five times faster. <bookmark mark='c'/> Replace the if with a mask, the comparison turned into all ones or all zeros, and there is nothing left to predict: the same speed on either data. <bookmark mark='d'/> Predictable branches are nearly free. Unpredictable ones in a hot loop are worth removing, and binary search's were not the bottleneck because the memory was.
ceda3a74afd0.zh: 无分支的查找在这个处理器上没有帮助，但这不意味着分支是免费的。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是一个循环，用一个 if 把数组中至少为一百二十八的字节加起来。<bookmark mark='b'/>在打乱的数据上，这个 if 就像抛硬币。第7和第8部分的预测器有一半时间猜错，每次猜错都要丢弃流水线推测执行的工作。在排好序的数据上，分支先一直走一边，再一直走另一边，几乎总能被预测对。同样的循环，同样的值，快了五倍。<bookmark mark='c'/>把 if 换成一个掩码，也就是把比较结果变成全一或全零，就没有什么需要预测了：在两种数据上速度相同。<bookmark mark='d'/>可预测的分支几乎是免费的。热循环中不可预测的分支值得去掉；而二分查找的分支之所以不是瓶颈，是因为瓶颈在内存。

951b9c256c9e.en: Chapter ten. Algorithm engineering, part two: vector instructions and hashing.
951b9c256c9e.zh: 第10章。算法工程（下）：向量指令与哈希。

9c6fe4591b0e.en: The Job spends much of its time finding words, one byte at a time. A modern core can look at thirty-two bytes in one instruction. <bookmark mark='a'/> Load thirty-two bytes. OR each with hexadecimal twenty, which lower-cases every letter, subtract the code for a, and the letters are exactly the bytes that come out at most twenty-five, all thirty-two compared at once. <bookmark mark='b'/> One more instruction, movemask, gathers the thirty-two answers into the bits of an ordinary integer. <bookmark mark='c'/> Now the word boundaries are bit tricks from chapter seven: a start is a letter whose left neighbour is not one, L and not L shifted. <bookmark mark='d'/> On the whole corpus, twenty-five megabytes, the byte-at-a-time loop takes forty milliseconds and the vector version four and a half: almost nine times faster, with the same counts. <bookmark mark='e'/> The simdjson library parses JSON at gigabytes per second with exactly these ideas.
9c6fe4591b0e.zh: Job 的大部分时间花在找单词上，一次一个字节。现代处理器的一条指令能同时看三十二个字节。<bookmark mark='a'/>载入三十二个字节。把每个字节与十六进制的二十做或运算，这会把每个字母变成小写；再减去 a 的编码，字母恰好就是结果不超过二十五的那些字节，三十二个一次比较完。<bookmark mark='b'/>再一条指令 movemask，把三十二个答案收集到一个普通整数的各个比特中。<bookmark mark='c'/>现在单词的边界就是第7章的比特技巧：一个词的开头是一个字母，而它左边的邻居不是字母，即 L 与 L 移位后的取反做与运算。<bookmark mark='d'/>在整个语料上，二十五兆字节，逐字节的循环要四十毫秒，向量版本四毫秒半：快了将近九倍，计数相同。<bookmark mark='e'/>simdjson 库正是用这些思想，以每秒几吉字节的速度解析 JSON。

9e48dd1919e3.en: Writing vector instructions by hand is a last resort. The compiler will often do it for you. <bookmark mark='a'/> The same three loops, compiled without and with vectorization. A scaled vector addition and a plain sum run about three times faster, because every iteration is independent and the compiler can pack eight or sixteen of them into each instruction. <bookmark mark='b'/> It can only do that when it can prove the arrays don't overlap, which is what the restrict keyword promises. <bookmark mark='c'/> A running prefix sum carries a dependency from each element to the next, so there is little to vectorize; it gains less, and only from unrolling. <bookmark mark='d'/> The practical rule: keep hot loops simple, over arrays, without hidden aliasing, and ask the compiler to report what it vectorized.
9e48dd1919e3.zh: 手写向量指令是最后的手段。编译器常常会替你完成。<bookmark mark='a'/>同样的三个循环，分别在不做和做向量化的情况下编译。带系数的向量加法和普通求和快了大约三倍，因为每次迭代都是独立的，编译器可以把八个或十六个迭代装进一条指令。<bookmark mark='b'/>只有当它能证明这些数组不重叠时才能这样做，而这正是 restrict 关键字所承诺的。<bookmark mark='c'/>累计前缀和在相邻元素之间有依赖，所以没有多少可以向量化的；它提升得更少，而且只来自循环展开。<bookmark mark='d'/>实用的规则是：让热循环保持简单，遍历数组，不要有隐藏的别名，并让编译器报告它向量化了什么。

a89fbb217d0f.en: Vector instructions also rebuilt the hash table. <bookmark mark='a'/> A Swiss table, Google's design from 2017, keeps a separate array of control bytes, one per slot, in groups of sixteen. An empty slot is marked; a full one stores seven bits of its key's hash. <bookmark mark='b'/> Part of the hash picks a group; the other seven bits are compared against all sixteen control bytes in one instruction, giving a mask of the few slots worth checking. Usually there is one, and it is the key. <bookmark mark='c'/> We timed three tables with sixteen million slots. <bookmark mark='d'/> Half full, the open-addressing tables are close. Seven eighths full, linear probing's clusters grow long and it falls behind by more than two and a half times, while the Swiss table barely notices: its probes stay short and inside one cache line. <bookmark mark='e'/> The standard library's chained map pays for a pointer chase on every node, the linked list of the opening chapter again. Abseil, Rust's standard HashMap and Facebook's F14 all use this design.
a89fbb217d0f.zh: 向量指令也重塑了哈希表。<bookmark mark='a'/>Swiss 表是谷歌2017年的设计，它另外保存一个控制字节数组，每个槽一个字节，十六个一组。空槽有标记；满的槽存放其键的哈希值的七个比特。<bookmark mark='b'/>哈希值的一部分选出一组；另外七个比特用一条指令与全部十六个控制字节比较，得到值得检查的少数几个槽的掩码。通常只有一个，而它就是那个键。<bookmark mark='c'/>我们给三种有一千六百万个槽的表计了时。<bookmark mark='d'/>半满时，开放寻址的两种表很接近。八分之七满时，线性探测的聚集变得很长，它落后了两倍半以上；而 Swiss 表几乎不受影响：它的探查很短，而且在一条缓存行之内。<bookmark mark='e'/>标准库的链式映射在每个节点上都要付出一次指针追逐，又是开头那一章的链表。Abseil、Rust 标准库的 HashMap 和 Facebook 的 F14 都采用了这种设计。

f67c9af5494e.en: What does a production sort actually do? <bookmark mark='a'/> The C++ standard library uses David Musser's introsort of 1997: quicksort, with the median of three elements as the pivot. <bookmark mark='b'/> If the recursion ever gets deeper than about twice log n, a sign of a bad input, it switches to heapsort, so the worst case is n log n after all. <bookmark mark='c'/> And below sixteen elements it finishes with insertion sort, which is quadratic and, at that size, fastest. <bookmark mark='d'/> Orson Peters' pattern-defeating quicksort, now in Go and Rust, also notices sorted runs and inputs designed to attack it. <bookmark mark='e'/> Python and Java use Timsort, which finds the runs already present in real data and merges them, galloping as in chapter six. <bookmark mark='f'/> Every one of them is the algorithms of Part 16, stitched together where measurements said the crossovers are.
f67c9af5494e.zh: 生产环境中的排序究竟在做什么？<bookmark mark='a'/>C++ 标准库使用 David Musser 1997年的内省排序：快速排序，以三个元素的中位数为枢轴。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果递归深度超过大约两倍 log n，这是输入不好的迹象，它就切换到堆排序，所以最坏情况终究是 n log n。<bookmark mark='c'/>而在少于十六个元素时，它用插入排序收尾；插入排序是平方的，但在这个规模上最快。<bookmark mark='d'/>Orson Peters 的模式击败快速排序，如今用在 Go 和 Rust 中，它还能识别已经有序的段和专门设计来攻击它的输入。<bookmark mark='e'/>Python 和 Java 使用 Timsort，它找出真实数据中已有的有序段并把它们归并，像第6章那样倍增查找。<bookmark mark='f'/>它们每一个都是第16部分的算法，在测量指出交叉点的地方缝合在一起。

5856e89282ee.en: Part 16 proved that sorting by comparisons needs n log n of them. <bookmark mark='a'/> Radix sort makes no comparisons. Least-significant-digit radix sort counts the keys by their lowest byte, moves them into place, and repeats for each of the four bytes: four linear passes for any number of keys. <bookmark mark='b'/> For sixteen keys it is far slower than the standard library's introsort, because each pass clears and scans two hundred and fifty-six counters. <bookmark mark='c'/> The two cross at about sixty-four keys on this machine. <bookmark mark='d'/> At sixteen million keys, radix sort is three and a half times faster, and its curve jumps when the arrays stop fitting in the cache, the hierarchy again. <bookmark mark='e'/> Real libraries are hybrids: radix for big integer arrays, insertion sort for tiny ones, vectorized quicksorts like Google's vqsort, and parallel in-place samplesorts like IPS4o.
5856e89282ee.zh: 第16部分证明了基于比较的排序需要 n log n 次比较。<bookmark mark='a'/>基数排序不做比较。最低位优先的基数排序按最低的字节给键计数，把它们放到位，再对四个字节逐一重复：无论多少个键，都只是四遍线性扫描。<bookmark mark='b'/>对十六个键，它比标准库的内省排序慢得多，因为每一遍都要清零并扫描二百五十六个计数器。<bookmark mark='c'/>在这台机器上，两者在大约六十四个键处交叉。<bookmark mark='d'/>在一千六百万个键时，基数排序快了三倍半；当数组不再装得进缓存时，它的曲线会跳一下，又是存储层次。<bookmark mark='e'/>真正的库都是混合的：大整数数组用基数排序，极小的用插入排序，还有谷歌的 vqsort 这样的向量化快速排序，以及 IPS4o 这样的并行原地样本排序。

e18fe9c16aad.en: Often you don't need the whole order. <bookmark mark='a'/> The Job only wants the twenty most common words, and here are four ways to find the twenty largest of sixteen million keys. <bookmark mark='b'/> Sorting everything takes over a second and a half. A heap of twenty, scanned once, compares each key with the heap's smallest member, almost always finds it smaller, and moves on: about seventeen milliseconds, a hundred times faster. The library's partial sort does the same. <bookmark mark='c'/> Quickselect, the library's nth element, is linear in theory but sweeps the whole array several times, so for a small k the heap wins. <bookmark mark='d'/> The lesson is older than computers: ask for what you need. The top k is a different and much easier problem than a sorted list.
e18fe9c16aad.zh: 很多时候你并不需要完整的顺序。<bookmark mark='a'/>Job 只要最常见的二十个词；这里有四种办法，找出一千六百万个键中最大的二十个。<bookmark mark='b'/>全部排序要一秒半以上。一个容量为二十的堆，扫描一遍，把每个键与堆中最小的成员比较，几乎总是发现它更小，然后继续：大约十七毫秒，快了一百倍。库里的 partial_sort 做的是同样的事。<bookmark mark='c'/>快速选择，也就是库里的 nth_element，理论上是线性的，但要把整个数组扫上好几遍，所以对于小的 k，堆胜出。<bookmark mark='d'/>这个道理比计算机还古老：只要你需要的东西。前 k 个是一个与排好序的列表不同、而且容易得多的问题。

712a340a7000.zh: 第12章。诚实地做基准测试。

eabc0387f91d.en: Every number in this part came from a stopwatch, so it is fair to ask how far to trust them. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is one small program run thirty times, timing the same loop six times inside each run. <bookmark mark='b'/> The first repetition is consistently slower, about a quarter, because the caches, the branch predictors and the page tables start cold, and the processor may still be raising its clock. Warm up before you measure. <bookmark mark='c'/> Even warm, the runs spread by more than ten percent. A single timing is an anecdote. Report the distribution, compare medians with confidence intervals, and keep repeating until the intervals are narrow enough to decide.
eabc0387f91d.zh: 这一部分的每个数字都来自一块秒表，所以有理由问：它们有多可信？<bookmark mark='a'/>这是一个小程序运行三十次，每次运行内部对同一个循环计时六次。<bookmark mark='b'/>第一次重复总是更慢，大约慢四分之一，因为缓存、分支预测器和页表都是冷的，处理器可能还在提升时钟频率。测量之前先预热。<bookmark mark='c'/>即使预热之后，各次运行的差别也超过百分之十。单次计时只是一则轶事。要报告分布，用置信区间比较中位数，并不断重复，直到区间窄到足以做出判断。

c4578a183abb.en: Two traps catch experienced engineers. <bookmark mark='a'/> The first is layout. We ran the same binary with nothing changed except the size of its environment variables, which shifts where the stack begins. The median moved by up to twenty-two percent. On a shared cloud machine part of that is noise from neighbours, and that is the point: without randomized layouts and many repetitions, a change of that size cannot be told apart from luck. <bookmark mark='b'/> Todd Mytkowicz and colleagues showed in 2009 that such accidents, the environment's size and even the order of object files at link time, can turn a measured speedup into a slowdown. Charlie Curtsinger and Emery Berger's Stabilizer re-randomizes the layout during a run, so that differences can be tested statistically. <bookmark mark='c'/> The second trap is the optimizer. This loop's result is never used, so the compiler deleted it: a hundred million iterations in a microsecond. <bookmark mark='d'/> Keep the result, and the same loop takes a hundred and twenty milliseconds. A benchmark whose output is unused may be measuring nothing.
c4578a183abb.zh: 有两个陷阱连有经验的工程师也会掉进去。<bookmark mark='a'/>第一个是布局。我们运行同一个二进制程序，只改变它环境变量的大小，这会移动栈开始的位置。中位数的变化最多达到百分之二十二。在共享的云机器上，其中一部分来自邻居的噪声，而这正是要点：没有随机化的布局和多次重复，这种幅度的变化无法与运气区分开。<bookmark mark='b'/>Todd Mytkowicz 和同事们在2009年表明，这类偶然因素，环境的大小，甚至链接时目标文件的顺序，都能把测得的加速变成减速。Charlie Curtsinger 和 Emery Berger 的 Stabilizer 在运行中不断重新随机化布局，从而可以对差异做统计检验。<bookmark mark='c'/>第二个陷阱是优化器。这个循环的结果从未被使用，所以编译器把它删掉了：一亿次迭代只用了一微秒。<bookmark mark='d'/>保留结果，同样的循环要一百二十毫秒。一个输出没被使用的基准测试，可能什么也没有测到。

c83a9d07e523.en: Chapter thirteen. Problem solving as a craft.

7db309553333.en: In 1945 George Pólya wrote a small book on how to solve mathematical problems, and it is still the best advice for algorithms. <bookmark mark='a'/> First, understand the problem: work three tiny examples by hand, and find the edge cases before they find you. <bookmark mark='b'/> Second, make a plan, and the most powerful question is: have I seen this before, in disguise? Booking meeting rooms is interval colouring; the cheapest way to connect cities is a spanning tree; a puzzle with a monotone answer is a binary search. <bookmark mark='c'/> Third, carry it out, and write the brute force first, because it is the reference you will test the fast version against. <bookmark mark='d'/> Fourth, look back: state the invariant, and stress-test the fast solution against the slow one on thousands of random inputs. <bookmark mark='e'/> That is how every structure in this part was checked.
7db309553333.zh: 1945年，George Pólya 写了一本关于如何解数学题的小书，至今仍是对算法最好的忠告。<bookmark mark='a'/>第一，理解问题：手算三个小例子，在边界情况找上你之前先找到它们。<bookmark mark='b'/>第二，拟订计划，而最有力的问题是：我以前见过它吗，换了装扮的它？预订会议室就是区间着色；连接城市最便宜的方式就是生成树；答案单调的谜题就是二分查找。<bookmark mark='c'/>第三，执行计划，先写暴力解法，因为它是你检验快速版本的参照。<bookmark mark='d'/>第四，回顾：写出不变式，并在成千上万个随机输入上用慢的解法对快的解法做压力测试。<bookmark mark='e'/>这一部分的每个结构都是这样检验的。

e42b94645bee.en: Here are the four steps on a small problem: count the pairs whose sum is at most T. <bookmark mark='a'/> Understand it with tiny cases: one, two, three with T equal to four gives two pairs; an empty array gives none. <bookmark mark='b'/> Plan. The pairs don't depend on the order, so sort. Then if the smallest remaining value plus the largest fits under T, so does the smallest plus everything in between: all those pairs at once. <bookmark mark='c'/> Carry it out: brute force first, then two pointers from the ends. If the pair fits, count j minus i and move i right; if not, move j left. <bookmark mark='d'/> Look back: two thousand random small inputs, and the fast version never disagreed with the slow one. Only then time it: on four thousand numbers in Python, four hundred milliseconds for the brute force, under one millisecond for the two pointers.
e42b94645bee.zh: 把这四步用在一个小问题上：数一数和不超过 T 的数对有多少。<bookmark mark='a'/>用很小的例子理解它：一、二、三，T 等于四，得到两对；空数组得到零对。<bookmark mark='b'/>拟订计划。数对与顺序无关，所以先排序。如果剩下的最小值加上最大值不超过 T，那么最小值加上中间的每一个也都不超过：这些数对一次全数上。<bookmark mark='c'/>执行：先写暴力解法，再从两端用双指针。如果这一对满足，就加上 j 减 i 并把 i 右移；否则把 j 左移。<bookmark mark='d'/>回顾：两千个随机的小输入，快的版本从未与慢的版本不一致。然后才去计时：在 Python 中对四千个数，暴力解法四百毫秒，双指针不到一毫秒。

399810464029.en: Programming interviews draw on a repertoire of about twenty patterns, and this course has now built all of them. <bookmark mark='a'/> Hash maps for counting, from Part 17; two pointers and sliding windows from this part; heaps for the top k; breadth-first and depth-first search and topological order from Part 18; union-find and spanning trees; dynamic programming and backtracking from Part 19; tries and string matching from Part 21; and the least-recently-used cache, a hash map threaded with a doubly linked list, which needed Part 9's hierarchy and Part 23's competitive analysis to justify. <bookmark mark='b'/> An interview tests fluency. The job tests judgment: which tool, and what it costs on a real machine, which is what the second half of this part measured. <bookmark mark='c'/> Steven Skiena's Algorithm Design Manual is a catalogue of problems in disguise, for when Pólya's second step needs help.
399810464029.zh: 编程面试依赖大约二十种模式，而这门课现在已经把它们全部构造出来了。<bookmark mark='a'/>用于计数的哈希表，来自第17部分；双指针和滑动窗口来自这一部分；求前 k 个用堆；广度优先、深度优先搜索和拓扑排序来自第18部分；并查集和生成树；动态规划和回溯来自第19部分；字典树和字符串匹配来自第21部分；还有最近最少使用缓存，一个用双向链表串起来的哈希表，它需要第9部分的存储层次和第23部分的竞争分析来说明其合理性。<bookmark mark='b'/>面试考的是熟练，工作考的是判断：用哪种工具，以及它在真实机器上的代价，这正是这一部分后半段测量的内容。<bookmark mark='c'/>Steven Skiena 的《算法设计手册》是一本换了装扮的问题目录，在 Pólya 的第二步需要帮助时可以翻一翻。

e0ed2ba2beb5.zh: 第14章。工程优化后的 Job。

b398c3dc70b6.en: The Job counts the words of thirty novels and lists the twenty most common. Part 17 did it with an open-addressing hash table, and we ran that program in C on this machine. Now we engineer it. <bookmark mark='a'/> First, find the words with the vector scan of chapter ten. <bookmark mark='b'/> Second, hash eight letters at a time with one multiplication instead of one letter per step. <bookmark mark='c'/> Third, a Swiss-style table, sixteen control bytes compared at once. <bookmark mark='d'/> And fourth, store the first eight letters, the length and the count inside the slot itself, so that a short word, which is most words, is found and counted without touching any other memory. <bookmark mark='e'/> Best of seven runs: a hundred and fifty-five milliseconds for the textbook version, seventy-five for the engineered one, about twice as fast, with identical output. <bookmark mark='f'/> The engineered runs varied a lot, so the honest claim is the best time and the median together. What is left is about one hash and one cache miss per word.
b398c3dc70b6.zh: Job 统计三十部小说中的单词，并列出最常见的二十个。第17部分用开放寻址哈希表做到了，我们在这台机器上用 C 语言运行了那个程序。现在我们对它做工程优化。<bookmark mark='a'/>第一，用第10章的向量扫描找单词。<bookmark mark='b'/>第二，用一次乘法一次哈希八个字母，而不是每步一个字母。<bookmark mark='c'/>第三，Swiss 风格的表，十六个控制字节一次比较。<bookmark mark='d'/>第四，把单词的前八个字母、长度和计数存在槽里，这样短单词，也就是大多数单词，不用碰任何其他内存就能被找到并计数。<bookmark mark='e'/>七次运行中最好的一次：教科书版本一百五十五毫秒，工程优化版本七十五毫秒，大约快一倍，输出完全相同。<bookmark mark='f'/>工程优化版本的各次运行差别很大，所以诚实的说法是同时给出最好时间和中位数。剩下的，大约是每个单词一次哈希和一次缓存缺失。

429c86c656b0.en: Before engineering anything, measure where the time goes. <bookmark mark='a'/> In the textbook program, finding the words took about a quarter of the time, and the hash table the rest. <bookmark mark='b'/> The vector scan makes the first part nine times faster. But on its own that would make the whole program only about thirty percent faster, because the table is untouched. That is Amdahl's law, from 1967: the part you do not speed up decides the total. <bookmark mark='c'/> So the table had to change as well, and the slot that carries the word's first letters is what took it from about a hundred and fifteen milliseconds to seventy. Profile first; then engineer the largest part.
429c86c656b0.zh: 在做任何工程优化之前，先测量时间花在哪里。<bookmark mark='a'/>在教科书程序中，找单词大约占四分之一的时间，其余是哈希表。<bookmark mark='b'/>向量扫描让前一部分快了九倍。但单靠它，整个程序只会快大约百分之三十，因为表没有动。这就是1967年的 Amdahl 定律：你没有加速的那部分决定了总体。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以表也必须改，正是那个带着单词前几个字母的槽，把它从大约一百一十五毫秒降到了七十毫秒。先做性能剖析，再优化最大的那部分。

b60ed270708f.en: So the ledger gets its tenth row, and it is a new kind of row. <bookmark mark='a'/> Rows one to nine priced the Job on the cores we built, from the single-cycle Pebble of Part 6 to the four cores of Part 10. Row ten is measured on the real processor that rendered this video. <bookmark mark='b'/> Part 17's textbook program alone runs five times faster here than on our modelled core, because a real core is wider, faster and has far larger caches. <bookmark mark='c'/> The engineering then doubles that again: seventy-five milliseconds for twenty-five megabytes. <bookmark mark='d'/> From two hundred and eighty-one seconds on the first row to seventy-five milliseconds, a factor of nearly four thousand, and every layer of the tower contributed to it.
b60ed270708f.zh: 于是账本有了第十行，而且是一种新的行。<bookmark mark='a'/>第一到第九行是在我们构造的处理器上给 Job 定价的，从第6部分的单周期 Pebble 到第10部分的四个核。第十行是在渲染这段视频的真实处理器上测量的。<bookmark mark='b'/>单是第17部分的教科书程序，在这里就比在我们建模的处理器上快五倍，因为真实的处理器更宽、更快，缓存也大得多。<bookmark mark='c'/>工程优化又让它快了一倍：二十五兆字节，七十五毫秒。<bookmark mark='d'/>从第一行的二百八十一秒到七十五毫秒，相差将近四千倍，而技术栈的每一层都为此做出了贡献。

a143507ddbdf.en: Chapter fifteen. Frontier: learned indexes, and algorithms with predictions.
a143507ddbdf.zh: 第15章。前沿：学习索引，与带预测的算法。

06397c15d164.en: The frontier has a simple question: what if a data structure could learn the shape of its data? <bookmark mark='a'/> Take the four point six million positions where words begin in our corpus, a sorted array of thirty-seven megabytes. <bookmark mark='b'/> A sorted array is a function from keys to positions, and this one is nearly a straight line. Fit it with line segments, each guaranteed to predict every position within epsilon. To look a key up, find its segment, predict, and binary-search only the small window around the prediction. <bookmark mark='c'/> Tim Kraska and colleagues at Google proposed learned indexes in 2018; Paolo Ferragina and Giorgio Vinciguerra's PGM index made the guarantees exact. <bookmark mark='d'/> Here sixty-four segments, a kilobyte and a half, index the whole array to within two hundred and fifty-six positions, and lookups are about one and a half times faster than binary search.
06397c15d164.zh: 前沿有一个简单的问题：如果一个数据结构能学会它的数据的形状会怎样？<bookmark mark='a'/>取我们语料中单词开始的四百六十万个位置，一个三十七兆字节的有序数组。<bookmark mark='b'/>有序数组是从键到位置的函数，而这个函数几乎是一条直线。用线段拟合它，每段都保证预测每个位置的误差在 epsilon 之内。查找一个键时，先找到它的线段，做出预测，然后只在预测附近的小窗口里二分查找。<bookmark mark='c'/>谷歌的 Tim Kraska 和同事们在2018年提出了学习索引；Paolo Ferragina 和 Giorgio Vinciguerra 的 PGM 索引让这些保证变得精确。<bookmark mark='d'/>这里六十四条线段，一千五百字节，就把整个数组索引到误差两百五十六个位置以内，而查找比二分查找快大约一倍半。

9cd347d1b501.en: Part 23's online algorithms assumed nothing about the future. In practice we often have a forecast. <bookmark mark='a'/> Give ski rental a prediction of the season's length, and a trust parameter lambda: if the forecast says long, buy after lambda B days; if short, wait until B over lambda. <bookmark mark='b'/> If the forecast is right the cost is at most one plus lambda times the best, and however wrong it is, never more than one plus one over lambda. <bookmark mark='c'/> With lambda a tenth and a perfect forecast we pay exactly what the clairvoyant pays; as the forecast's error grows, the cost rises gracefully, and the worst case stays bounded. With lambda equal to one we are back at Part 23's break-even rule, which ignores the forecast. <bookmark mark='d'/> Manish Purohit, Zoya Svitkina and Ravi Kumar, and Thodoris Lykouris and Sergei Vassilvitskii for caching, started this field in 2018: use machine learning when it is right, and keep a worst-case guarantee when it is not.
9cd347d1b501.zh: 第23部分的在线算法对未来不做任何假设。在实践中，我们常常有一个预测。<bookmark mark='a'/>给租雪板问题一个雪季长度的预测，以及一个信任参数 lambda：如果预测说长，就在 lambda 乘以 B 天后买；如果说短，就等到 B 除以 lambda 天。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果预测正确，花费至多是最优的一加 lambda 倍；无论预测错得多离谱，都不超过一加 lambda 分之一倍。<bookmark mark='c'/>lambda 取十分之一、预测完全正确时，我们付的恰好和先知一样；随着预测误差增大，花费平缓上升，而最坏情况始终有界。lambda 等于一时，我们就回到了第23部分那条忽略预测的盈亏平衡规则。<bookmark mark='d'/>Manish Purohit、Zoya Svitkina 和 Ravi Kumar，以及研究缓存的 Thodoris Lykouris 和 Sergei Vassilvitskii，在2018年开创了这个领域：机器学习正确时就利用它，不正确时也保留最坏情况的保证。

76133e4abe73.en: Underneath this whole part runs a gap between theory and practice. <bookmark mark='a'/> Four searches with exactly the same comparisons differ fivefold on sixty-four million keys. <bookmark mark='b'/> The random-access machine of Part 16 counts operations; real machines charge for distance. <bookmark mark='c'/> Alok Aggarwal and Jeffrey Vitter's external-memory model counts the transfers of blocks between a small fast memory and a large slow one. <bookmark mark='d'/> The cache-oblivious model of Matteo Frigo, Charles Leiserson and colleagues asks for algorithms that are optimal for every block size at once, without knowing it, like the van Emde Boas tree layout. <bookmark mark='e'/> Neither captures prefetching, vector units or branch prediction, which decided several of this part's measurements. A model simple enough to reason with and accurate enough to rank real implementations is still missing.
76133e4abe73.zh: 在这整个部分之下，贯穿着理论与实践之间的差距。<bookmark mark='a'/>比较次数完全相同的四种查找，在六千四百万个键上相差五倍。<bookmark mark='b'/>第16部分的随机存取机计算操作次数；真实的机器按距离收费。<bookmark mark='c'/>Alok Aggarwal 和 Jeffrey Vitter 的外存模型计算的是数据块在小而快的存储器与大而慢的存储器之间的传输次数。<bookmark mark='d'/>Matteo Frigo、Charles Leiserson 及同事们的缓存无关模型，要求算法在不知道块大小的情况下对每种块大小同时最优，比如 van Emde Boas 树布局。<bookmark mark='e'/>两者都没有刻画预取、向量单元或分支预测，而这些决定了这一部分好几项测量的结果。一个既简单到可以推理、又准确到能给真实实现排出名次的模型，至今仍然缺失。

1fd6cac92995.en: Here is where things stand. <bookmark mark='a'/> Is there a cost model that ranks real implementations correctly, accounting for caches, prefetching, vector units and branches, and is still simple enough to prove things in? <bookmark mark='b'/> Can learned indexes keep worst-case guarantees when keys are inserted, or chosen by an adversary? <bookmark mark='c'/> And a puzzle from our own measurements. Ferragina, Lillo and Vinciguerra proved that if the gaps between keys are independent, the segments grow like epsilon squared. On our corpus they grow more slowly, roughly like epsilon to the one point four. Why? <bookmark mark='d'/> This part's research problem takes the third.
1fd6cac92995.zh: 现状如下。<bookmark mark='a'/>是否存在一个代价模型，能正确地给真实实现排名，考虑到缓存、预取、向量单元和分支，同时又简单到可以在其中证明东西？<bookmark mark='b'/>当键被插入，或由对手选择时，学习索引还能保持最坏情况的保证吗？<bookmark mark='c'/>还有一个来自我们自己测量的谜题。Ferragina、Lillo 和 Vinciguerra 证明，如果键之间的间隔是独立的，线段的长度按 epsilon 的平方增长。在我们的语料上，它增长得更慢，大约是 epsilon 的一点四次方。为什么？<bookmark mark='d'/>这一部分的研究题选的是第三个。

83949e404aa8.en: What we built in this part. Prefix sums and difference arrays, and the integral image. Fenwick trees from a single bit trick, and segment trees for any associative operation, lazily. Sparse tables, lowest common ancestors and the Cartesian tree that makes them the same problem. Two pointers, monotonic stacks and binary search on the answer. Bit tricks, submasks and the Four Russians; meet in the middle and square roots. Then the machine: two linear loops a hundred and forty times apart, search layouts, vector scans, Swiss tables and radix sort, all measured honestly, and the Job at seventy-five milliseconds.
83949e404aa8.zh: 这一部分我们构造了什么。前缀和与差分数组，以及积分图。由一个比特技巧得来的 Fenwick 树，以及适用于任何结合律运算、带懒惰传播的线段树。稀疏表、最近公共祖先，以及让二者成为同一问题的 Cartesian 树。双指针、单调栈和二分答案。比特技巧、子掩码和四个俄罗斯人算法；折半搜索和平方根分块。然后是机器：相差一百四十倍的两个线性循环，查找布局、向量扫描、Swiss 表和基数排序，全都诚实地测量过，以及跑到七十五毫秒的 Job。

560608f54a80.en: Where this comes back. Part 35's database indexes a billion rows with three levels of a B-plus tree, the layout of chapter nine, and executes queries in vectors. Part 41 finds merge bases as lowest common ancestors. Part 46 scans columnar files with vector instructions. Part 47's search engine gallops through posting lists and decodes them with SIMD. Part 48 measures tail latency under load, which needs the benchmarking of chapter twelve. And Part 60's roofline model makes this part's lesson exact: most programs are limited by memory, not by arithmetic.
560608f54a80.zh: 它们会在哪里再出现。第35部分的数据库用三层 B+ 树索引十亿行，正是第9章的布局，并以向量方式执行查询。第41部分把合并基点当作最近公共祖先来求。第46部分用向量指令扫描列式文件。第47部分的搜索引擎在倒排表中倍增查找，并用 SIMD 解码它们。第48部分测量负载下的尾延迟，这需要第12章的基准测试方法。而第60部分的屋顶线模型把这一部分的教训变得精确：大多数程序受限于内存，而不是算术。

c78de46b403b.en: In practice. Interviews test the patterns of chapter thirteen, with their costs and edge cases. Databases and search engines are built from B-plus trees, bitmaps, galloping intersections and vector scans. Games and exchanges keep leaderboards and order books in Fenwick and segment trees. And performance work on a hot path starts with a profiler and an honest benchmark, and usually ends with a better memory layout.
c78de46b403b.zh: 在实践中。面试考第13章的那些模式，以及它们的代价和边界情况。数据库和搜索引擎由 B+ 树、位图、倍增求交和向量扫描构成。游戏和交易所用 Fenwick 树和线段树维护排行榜和订单簿。而热路径上的性能优化，从性能剖析器和诚实的基准测试开始，通常以更好的内存布局结束。

2a093f05f365.en: Six problems, with full solutions in the part's notes. Pause on any of them. The fifth is a build problem: a Fenwick tree in the Pebble language, run on the emulator over the Job's own counts. The last, marked with a star, is a research problem: its answer is not known, and the notes say where to start.
2a093f05f365.zh: 六道习题，完整解答在这一部分的笔记里。可以在任何一道上暂停。第五道是构造题：用 Pebble 语言写一棵 Fenwick 树，在模拟器上基于 Job 自己的计数运行。最后一道标有星号，是研究题：它的答案尚不知道，笔记里说明了从哪里入手。

b0777746700d.en: Next time, Act Five begins, with limits. Part 1 proved that one problem cannot be solved. Part 25 finds the same impossibility everywhere: in every non-trivial question about what programs do, in equations over the integers, in tilings of the plane, and in Gödel's theorem, all from the fact that a program can print its own source. And the busy beaver marks the place where proof itself runs out. Part 25, Undecidable.
b0777746700d.zh: 下一次，第五幕开始，讲的是极限。第1部分证明了有一个问题无法解决。第25部分会在各处发现同样的不可能性：在关于程序行为的每个非平凡问题中，在整数上的方程中，在平面的铺砌中，在哥德尔定理中，而这一切都源于一个程序能打印出自己的源代码。忙碌海狸则标出了证明本身走到尽头的地方。第25部分，不可判定。

9bd24692775d.en: The books and papers this part follows are on screen and in the notes. Thank you for watching.
9bd24692775d.zh: 这一部分所依据的书和论文都在屏幕上，也在笔记里。感谢观看。
